title: The self made of food
hookLine: the Taittiriya's outermost layer of a person is made of food, and it calls food the eldest of beings
carry: the body is the first self, made of food

lines: THE OUTERMOST IS MADE OF FOOD.
cards: Open a set of nesting dolls. Inside the big painted one, a smaller one; inside that, a smaller one, finer and finer, until you reach the tiny one in the middle.

The Taittiriya Upanishad's second book takes a person apart the same way, five layers deep, and the next three days open them one by one. Today, the outermost doll. It's made of something you ate this week.

teach.b: The book opens with a promise: the one who knows Brahman reaches the highest. And a definition in four Sanskrit words: satyam jnanam anantam brahma. Brahman is truth, knowledge, the infinite.
Then a creation story, told like a relay. From this self, space came.

teach.h: SPACE, WIND, FIRE, WATER, EARTH, FOOD.
teach.b: From space, wind. From wind, fire. From fire, water.
From water, earth. From earth, plants. From plants, food.
From food, the person. So the person, the text says, is made of the essence of food. Annamaya: made of food.
And it draws that person as a bird. This is the head. This is the right wing.
This is the left wing. This is the body. This, underneath, is the tail, the foundation.
Then a short hymn to food. From food all creatures are born. By food they live.
Into food, in the end, they go. Food is the eldest of beings, so it's called the medicine of everything.

teach.h: THE PERSON MADE OF FOOD, SHAPED LIKE A BIRD.
teach.b: Hindu homes treat food as something holy, offered to God before anyone eats and shared back as prasad, and this hymn shows how deep that runs: food isn't only fuel, it's what a person is made of.
And it's something you can check. The hands holding your phone were, not long ago, rice, lentils, bread, an apple.
And then the text says: different from this one made of food, inside it, is another self, made of breath.
That's tomorrow. Later Hindu teachers call these layers the five koshas, the five sheaths, like a sword's scabbard. The Taittiriya itself doesn't use that word.
It just keeps saying: inside this one, another self.

how: Many Hindus offer food to God before eating and receive it back as prasad; in Vedanta and in yoga teaching, the five koshas drawn from this Upanishad are used to describe the layers of a person, starting with the body made of food.

o: a fasting vow kept before worship
a feast given to guests at the door
made of food: the body, the outermost layer

games.q: what's inside the teaching — tap the pairs.
p: a later name: sheath, like a scabbard

s: the Taittiriya itself calls the layers the five koshas
the word kosha comes from later teachers; the text just says: inside this one, another self.
the text draws the person made of food as a bird
head, right wing, left wing, body, and the tail as foundation.
food is called the medicine of everything
because it is the eldest of beings.

games.q: the relay of creation: from the self, space; from space, wind; then fire, water, earth, plants. what comes from plants?
o: food, and from food, the person.
games.why: from plants, food; from food, the person. so the person is annamaya, made of the essence of food.

practice: Feel the body's weight on the seat, its warmth, its pulse, the heaviness of the hands, and remember, gently, that this was food: grain, fruit, water, sunlight, a farmer's work, someone's cooking.
Let a little thanks go to all of it, then feel the body again just as it is, the first layer, the one you can touch.

wordCard.voice: Annamaya, made of food. In the Taittiriya, the outermost self: the body, built from what a person eats, and the first of the five layers.

orig.note: Sanskrit anna (food) + maya (made of): the self made of food, the body.

carryVoice: Your line: the body is the first self, made of food. Food is the eldest of beings. That's day three hundred ninety-one.

sources.ref: Taittiriya Upanishad 2.1–2.2 (the relay of creation; the person made of food; the hymn to food)
